lessons.title: A route and its conditions
lessons.description: Follow landmarks, recognise a closed passage and form conditional attachments.

grammar.title: Describe a regular result or a discovery
grammar.formation: Nonpast dictionary/ない verb or い-adjective + と. Noun/な-adjective + だと; negative でないと. The result clause supplies tense.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 6. Use と for an explained route, an automatic response or a regular result. It can also introduce a discovery after an actual event. A conditional does not certify a universal real-world guarantee. In this unit a route statement reports what is visible, while a one-off request after arrival uses たら.
grammar.example: 横断歩道を渡ると、青い看板が見えます。
grammar.translation: When you cross the pedestrian crossing, the blue sign is visible.

examples.ja: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}ると、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えます。
examples.en: When you cross the pedestrian crossing, the blue sign is visible.

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{暗|くら}いと、{矢印|やじるし}が{見|み}えにくいです。
examples.en: When the road is dark, the arrow is difficult to see.

examples.ja: {地図|ちず}を{開|ひら}くと、{裏側|うらがわ}にも{説明|せつめい}がありました。
examples.en: When I opened the map, there were instructions on the reverse side too.

grammar.mistake: Do not use automatic-result と as the after-arrival link in a one-off instruction such as “when you arrive, please message me”. A past discovery is not a habitual result or a chosen action sequence.

grammar.title: Form the condition; check the subject and result
grammar.formation: Godan final u-row → e-row + ば; ichidan drop る + れば; する→すれば; 来る→来れば (くれば). い-adjective い→ければ, いい→よければ; negative ない→なければ. Noun/な-adjective + ならば/であれば; negative でなければ.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 10 and its earlier regret pattern. ば presents a condition for a result; it is not an English “if and only if”. たら can overlap. Wishes/requests can follow state, potential or negative conditions, and different actors permit cases that a simplistic blanket ban would reject. For a single actor’s successive actions and a request, practice たら in lesson two.
grammar.example: 歩道を通れば、店に行けます。
grammar.translation: If you take the sidewalk, you can get to the café.

examples.ja: {歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}れば、{店|みせ}に{行|い}けます。
examples.en: If you take the sidewalk, you can get to the café.

examples.ja: {目印|めじるし}が{分|わ}からなければ、{地図|ちず}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.en: If you do not know the landmark, please check the map.

examples.ja: {時間|じかん}があれば、{二|ふた}つの{経路|けいろ}を{比|くら}べたいです。
examples.en: If there is time, I would like to compare two routes.

grammar.mistake: 書く→書けば, not 書くば; 食べる→食べれば. Never mark ば wrong merely because the result includes a request: the type of condition and the actors matter. Scored form practice names the required pattern.

grammar.title: An action after arrival, or a hypothetical case
grammar.formation: Plain past + ら: た→たら and だ→だら. Noun/な-adjective だったら; い-adjective かったら; いい→よかったら; negative なかったら. Past morphology does not itself set calendar time.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 5. たら can give a condition, an after-completion sequence, a one-off discovery, or a hypothetical situation. In the travel request, reaching the destination happens before sending the arrival message. For negative conditions, the sense is “if not”, not “after not doing”. The surrounding dates decide future or past.
grammar.example: 店に着いたら、メッセージを送ってください。
grammar.translation: When you arrive at the café, please send a message.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。
examples.en: When you arrive at the café, please send a message.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}だったら、バスの{運行|うんこう}を{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: If the train service is suspended, I will check bus operations.

examples.ja: {終点|しゅうてん}で{降|お}りたら、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えました。
examples.en: When I got off at the last stop, the blue sign was visible.

grammar.mistake: Do not translate future 着いたら as “after you arrived yesterday”. The だ ending also occurs in verb past forms: 読んだ→読んだら. The train suspension in the scene is a contingency, not a reported fact.

grammar.title: Advice based on a stated plan
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + (の)なら. Noun/な-adjective + なら, with no inserted だ in simple 雨なら/便利なら. Clause + のなら adds a nominalised premise.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 1. Respond to the supplied plan or case: Misaki says she will take a bus, so Kenta recommends checking the timetable before boarding. The advice need not wait until the condition’s action happens. なら can also refer back to something already done; it is not a universal future-only form.
grammar.example: バスで来るなら、乗る前に運賃を調べてください。
grammar.translation: If you are coming by bus, please check the fare before boarding.

examples.ja: バスで{来|く}るなら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{運賃|うんちん}を{調|しら}べてください。
examples.en: If you are coming by bus, please check the fare before boarding.

examples.ja: {終点|しゅうてん}なら、{店|みせ}まで{歩|ある}けます。
examples.en: If you mean the last stop, you can walk to the café from there.

examples.ja: もう{確認|かくにん}したのなら、その{結果|けっか}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: If you have already checked, please tell me the result.

grammar.mistake: バスで来るなら can lead to advice before travel; バスで来たら can make that advice too late when it must precede boarding. Do not insert だ into the simple noun pattern or assume the journey has already happened.

dialogues.title: A route with a closed passage
dialogues.scene: On Friday Misaki asks Bao for directions to Saturday’s permitted café film gathering. Bao describes the station route and the current closed passage. This is route planning, not a report that Misaki has arrived.

lines.romaji: Ashita no eiga o miru kai ni sanka shitai desu. Mise made no michijun o oshiete kudasai.
lines.meaning: I would like to join tomorrow’s film gathering. Please tell me the route to the café.

lines.meaning: Permission has been obtained, and it starts at three. Please leave through the station’s east exit.

lines.meaning: It is opposite the bank. The nearby passage is closed, so you can get there by taking the sidewalk.

dialogues.title: Before boarding and after arrival
dialogues.scene: Still on Friday, Misaki tells Kenta she plans to take a bus tomorrow. Timetable, fare and boarding-point advice happens before travel. An arrival message happens after reaching the café. A stopped train is only a contingency.

lines.romaji: Ashita wa basu de koyō to omotte imasu. Jikokuhyō wa mada mite imasen.
lines.meaning: I am thinking of coming by bus tomorrow. I have not looked at the timetable yet.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: バスで{来|く}るなら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{時刻表|じこくひょう}と{運賃|うんちん}を{調|しら}べてください。
lines.romaji: Basu de kuru nara, noru mae ni jikokuhyō to unchin o shirabete kudasai.
lines.meaning: If you are coming by bus, please check the timetable and fare before boarding.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {乗|の}り{場|ば}も{先|さき}に{確認|かくにん}します。{終点|しゅうてん}で{降|お}りればいいんですね。
lines.romaji: Noriba mo saki ni kakunin shimasu. Shūten de orireba ii n desu ne.
lines.meaning: I will check the boarding point first too. I should get off at the last stop, right?

lines.line: はい。{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。{到着|とうちゃく}してからでいいですよ。
lines.romaji: Hai. Mise ni tsuitara, messēji o okutte kudasai. Tōchaku shite kara de ii desu yo.
lines.meaning: Yes. When you arrive at the café, please send a message. After arrival is fine.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {分|わ}かりました。もし{電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}だったら、バスの{運行|うんこう}を{確認|かくにん}します。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Moshi densha ga unkyū dattara, basu no unkō o kakunin shimasu.
lines.meaning: Understood. If the train service is suspended, I will check bus operations.

lines.speaker: Kenta

lines.romaji: Sore wa kari no baai desu ne. Ima, unkyū shite iru to iu renraku wa arimasen.
lines.meaning: That is a hypothetical case. We have no message saying that the service is suspended now.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {店|みせ}までの{通路|つうろ}は{使|つか}えません。{少|すこ}し{遠回|とおまわ}りですが、{歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}ってください。
lines.romaji: Mise made no tsūro wa tsukaemasen. Sukoshi tōmawari desu ga, hodō o tōtte kudasai.
lines.meaning: The passage to the café cannot be used. It is a little longer, but please take the sidewalk.

lines.line: {字幕|じまく}の{比較|ひかく}は、もう{終|お}わりましたか？
lines.romaji: Jimaku no hikaku wa, mō owarimashita ka?
lines.meaning: Is the subtitle comparison finished now?

lines.romaji: Hai. Onaji jōken de futatsu no gamen o kurabemashita. Junbi no buntan mo kakunin shimashita. Kaizen no an mo kentō shite imasu.

{近|ちか}くの{通路|つうろ}は{閉|し}まっているので、{歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}れば{行|い}けます。{目印|めじるし}が{分|わ}からなければ、{安全|あんぜん}な{場所|ばしょ}で{地図|ちず}を{見|み}てください。{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。{道順|みちじゅん}を{調|しら}べるのは{出発|しゅっぱつ}する{前|まえ}、メッセージを{送|おく}るのは{到着|とうちゃく}した{後|あと}です。{映画|えいが}の{字幕|じまく}は、{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べます。

exercises.prompt: Which route does Bao describe after leaving the east exit?
options: Cross the crossing, turn right and look for the blue sign
Turn left without crossing and enter the closed passage
Go to the university and wait until next month
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly gives the crossing, right turn and blue sign.

exercises.prompt: Why should Misaki take the sidewalk?
options: The nearby passage is closed
The café has no permission
The film gathering has been cancelled
exercises.explain: Bao says the passage is closed and the sidewalk reaches the café.

options: Opposite the bank
Inside the station’s ticket office
Behind the university library
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says 銀行の向かい; the other places are not stated.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the dictionary form before route-result と. Do not choose between different valid conditionals.
exercises.line: {右|みぎ}に＿＿と、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えます。
options: {曲|ま}がる
{曲|ま}がって
{曲|ま}がります
exercises.explain: Dictionary 曲がる attaches to と; polite ます and て do not form this route construction.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named negative condition 分からなければ. Change ない to なければ.
exercises.line: {目印|めじるし}が＿＿、{地図|ちず}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
options: {分|わ}からなければ
{分|わ}からないば
{分|わ}からなくば
exercises.explain: 分からない→分からなければ. The request follows a negative condition; there is no blanket request ban.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Bao by accepting the stated closed-passage detour.
exercises.line: {近|ちか}くの{通路|つうろ}は{閉|し}まっています。
options: {分|わ}かりました。{歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}って{行|い}きます。
{分|わ}かりました。その{通路|つうろ}を{使|つか}います。
{分|わ}かりました。{映画|えいが}は{昨年|さくねん}{見|み}ました。
exercises.explain: Only the sidewalk reply accepts the route instruction; one contradicts it and one changes the subject.

exercises.meaning: When you cross the pedestrian crossing and turn right, the blue sign is visible.
tiles: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}って
exercises.explain: Crossing and turning precede the visible landmark; this is a route result.

exercises.prompt: What should Misaki check before boarding?
options: The timetable, fare and boarding point
The film ending and next year’s survey
Only the café’s arrival message
exercises.explain: Kenta names timetable and fare, and Misaki explicitly adds the boarding point.

exercises.prompt: When should Misaki send the arrival message?
options: After reaching the café
Before she has chosen any transport
Only after the film next year
exercises.explain: Kenta states 店に着いたら and 到着してから, making the sequence explicit.

exercises.prompt: What is the status of the stopped-train case?
options: It is hypothetical; no current suspension message is reported
It is confirmed that every train is stopped
It proves that the bus is cancelled
exercises.explain: Kenta calls it a hypothetical case and says no current suspension message has arrived; a conditional is not an announcement of a fact.

exercises.prompt: What responsibility and deadline does Kenta confirm on Friday?
options: Kenta handles registration due today, and two people will check responsibilities
Bao alone handles registration next month
Misaki has already cancelled every registration
exercises.explain: The final line names 申し込み, says its 期限 is 今日 on Friday, and states 二人で責任を確認します.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the past-plus-ら arrival form 着いたら, for a future message after arrival.
exercises.line: {店|みせ}に＿＿、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。
options: {着|つ}いたら
{着|つ}いてら
{着|つ}きたら
exercises.explain: 着く has plain past 着いた; adding ら gives 着いたら. The future plan fixes time.

exercises.context: Form practice: the stated plan is travel by bus. Supply the dictionary form before なら; check fares before boarding.
exercises.line: バスで＿＿なら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{運賃|うんちん}を{調|しら}べてください。
options: {来|く}る
{来|き}ます
{来|き}て
exercises.explain: 来るなら refers to the plan; the explicit 前 phrase locates preparation before travel.

exercises.context: Reply politely: accept timetable preparation before travel and a message after reaching the café.
exercises.line: バスで{来|く}るなら、{先|さき}に{時刻表|じこくひょう}を{見|み}てください。{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。
options: はい。{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{確認|かくにん}して、{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いてから{送|おく}ります。
はい。{到着|とうちゃく}してから{初|はじ}めて{時刻表|じこくひょう}を{調|しら}べます。
はい。まだ{着|つ}いていませんが、{到着|とうちゃく}したと{送|おく}ります。
exercises.explain: The first preserves both stated steps. The others postpone preparation or falsely claim arrival.

exercises.meaning: If you are coming by bus, please check the timetable before boarding.
tiles: {確認|かくにん}してください。
exercises.explain: The advice depends on the stated plan but occurs before boarding, not after the journey.

options: Check travel details → take the bus → reach the café → send a message
Send a completed-arrival message → choose a bus → start travel
Reach the café → check the boarding point for the first time
exercises.explain: 乗る前 and 着いたら, then the final before/after comparison, state this order.
exercises.context: Read the timing, not only the familiar transport words.

exercises.prompt: Which location and landmark are stated?
options: Opposite the bank, with a blue sign
Inside the university, with a red flag
At the first bus stop, with a yellow screen
exercises.explain: The first paragraph states 青い看板 and 銀行の向かい.

exercises.prompt: Which detail must readers look up because the guide does not supply it?
options: The fare and timetable for their bus
The café gathering’s starting time
Which way to turn after crossing
exercises.explain: The guide requests fare/timetable checks but gives no amounts or bus times; it states three o’clock and a right turn.
exercises.context: Separate supplied facts from a requested lookup.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a conditional line from your own clip. Note the actors, whether it is a fact or hypothesis, and whether advice happens before or after the condition. Saved examples are evidence, not a proficiency score.
